Singana Venkata Subbama vs Sri Sashibushan Kumar,Ias on 9
November, 2023
Author: R Raghunandan Rao

Bench: R Raghunandan Rao
 High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravathi
 Main Case No.CC.No.1166 of 2023
 Proceeding Sheet
Sl. Office
No Date Order Note
10 09.11.2023 Rrr, J

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravathi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioners had been assigned lands in  various survey numbers of Varikunta village,
 Atloor Mandal, Kadapa District.
Thereafter, a  proposal was moved to use these lands for an  irrigation project.

On the basis of the requisition  sent by the Executive Engineer, SP Division No.II,
 Nellore, proceedings dated 02.08.2013 were issued  by the Special Deputy Collector (LA), S.S.P, Unit-  IV, Rajampet, resuming an extent of Ac.63.53  cents from 26 assignees.
The said proceedings also  record that the lands have been resumed and  transfered to the Irrigation and Power Department.

As the petitioners were not being paid any  compensation or exgratia, in relation to these  lands, the petitioners had approached this Court,
 by way of W.P.No.5529 of 2019 which was  disposed of by an order dated 27.07.2022 with the  following directions:
 "Therefore, there shall be a direction to the  respondents to take steps in accordance with Act 30 of 2013 for payment of compensation and to act in terms of the letters dated 02.08.2013 addressed by the Special Deputy Collector (LA) and also the letter dated 20.07.2017 bearing reference No.G/80/2011.
This entire exercise should be completed within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs."
Since the said order was not complied, the petitioners had approached this Court, by way of the present contempt case.

The respondents have now taken the plea that the Requisition Department has reduced the extent of land required from Ac.63.53 cents of land to Ac.8.35 cents and consequently there was no need for acquisition or payment of compensation.

sentences.text: Smt. A. Sree Jayanthi, learned counsel appearing for the respondents would also contend that the petitioners remain in possession of the land and as such no loss would be suffered by the petitioners if the land is not taken over by the Government or compensation is not paid.
Sri S. Lakshmi Narayana Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the land has been submerged and the petitioners are not in possession of the said land.
He would further submit that that the respondents having resumed the land by proceedings of 2013, cannot leave the petitioners in Limbo.

He would further submit that unless the resumption proceedings are cancelled or a fresh assignment is made to the petitioners, they would have no title over the land and would be encroachers, even if it is taken that the petitioners are still in possession of the land.
In the circumstances, it is for the respondents to explain as to why the resumption proceedings have not been cancelled either by way of orders of cancellation or fresh assignment of land.
The other dispute that also requires to be looked into is the question of whether the petitioners are still in possession of the land or not.
Respondents 2 and 4 have appeared before this Court earlier.
However, it appears that the question of cancellation of resumption can only be answered by the 1st respondent.
In the circumstances, the 1st respondent shall be personally present on the next date of hearing before this Court.
